title: I Let the Splash-Pad Adult-Hours Sign Catch the Coach Who Ran Drills

parts.text: Adult hours started at 7:00 p.m. and coach Britt had a whistle drill in the pad at 7:06 with a youth team. The sign said: ADULT HOURS 7–8. NO TEAM DRILLS. I was forty, neighbor, holding a towel. Britt kept whistling. "Coaches are adults of the pad." I photographed the sign, the time, and the cones. Then I logged a drill. At 7:12 parks asked why Britt's cones were on adult hours. I asked once, then I documented twice. The second photo is for the person who will say they never saw the first.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Parks can see Britt's cones and whistle on the pad after 7 against the adult-hours sign.

social.video_title: The coach ran youth drills into adult hours — Part 1/2
social.description: Splash pad, a 7 p.m. sign, and a whistle. I logged the drill. Would you have photographed the cones?

parts.text: Britt called it cooldown until parks asked for the log. I printed the drill, the photo, and the sign. Cones left. Britt cooled on the lawn and told the team cooldown was always about optics. Optics is a word coaches use when a whistle exists. Adult hours now have a second line: TEAMS ARE NOT ADULTS. I keep 7–8. Britt lawns. The pad finally looks like water, not a practice. The room sounds like a room again, not a title. Petty is a word people use when their name is on the ticket.

social.description: Drill log, lawn cooldown, and a second line. Was cooldown ever a whistle after 7?
